contract: Bosch Motorsport Steering Wheel Angle Sensor LWS, order number F02U.V02.894-01
sourceDocument: Bosch Motorsport datasheet "Steering Wheel Angle Sensor LWS", document 54425995, en, 26 Aug 2025
derivation: Hand-derived from the Bosch datasheet tables only. NOT produced by running or transcribing the MFE26-VC LWSSteering decoder or the inverter_hil packLws encoder.
byteOrder: little-endian ("Byte order LSB (Intel)", CAN Parameters table). Explicitly stated by the datasheet, unlike the MTi.
bitrate: 500 kbaud (stated twice: Electrical Data and CAN Parameters)
layout: byte 0-1 LWS_ANGLE int16 LE, byte 2 LWS_SPEED uint8, byte 3 bit2 TRIM / bit1 CAL / bit0 OK with bits 7:3 reserved, byte 4 reserved
scaling: LWS_ANGLE 0.1 deg/count, LWS_SPEED 4 deg/s per count. See mti680_can_contract.md ASSUMPTION A7: the datasheet gives these as "Absolute physical resolution", not as an explicit LSB scaling.
invalidSentinels: LWS_ANGLE = 0x7FFF and LWS_SPEED = 0xFF whenever the truth table says the value is not valid

standardFrames.name: lws_speed_508dps
standardFrames.note: speed count 127 = 0x7F, the last value that survives an int8 cast

standardFrames.name: lws_speed_512dps
standardFrames.note: speed count 128 = 0x80. LWS_SPEED is UNSIGNED; an int8 receiver reads -128 here. First value that breaks a signed receiver.

standardFrames.name: lws_speed_max_1016dps
standardFrames.note: speed count 254 = 0xFE, top of the documented 0..1016 deg/s range. An int8 receiver reads -2.

standardFrames.name: lws_uncalibrated
standardFrames.note: Truth table row TRIM=1 OK=1 CAL=0: LWS_ANGLE is forced to the 0x7FFF sentinel, LWS_SPEED stays valid.

standardFrames.name: lws_failure_trim_only
standardFrames.note: Truth table row TRIM=1 OK=0 CAL=0: angle 0x7FFF, speed 0xFF, sensor in failure mode.

standardFrames.name: lws_failure_all_clear
standardFrames.note: Truth table row TRIM=0 OK=0 CAL=0: angle 0x7FFF, speed 0xFF, sensor in failure mode.

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_invalid_short_dlc
invalidAndEdge.expectation: REJECT. LWS_Standard is a 5-byte message (Bosch F02U.V02.894-01, CAN Message table).

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_invalid_long_dlc
invalidAndEdge.expectation: REJECT or accept-first-5 - the datasheet fixes the length at 5 and says nothing about padding. The MFE26-VC driver requires length == 5 exactly, so a simulator MUST emit DLC 5.

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_invalid_status_combo_010
invalidAndEdge.expectation: REJECT. TRIM=0 CAL=1 OK=0 is listed under "Other combinations for TRIM, OK and CAL are not valid".

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_invalid_status_combo_011
invalidAndEdge.expectation: REJECT. TRIM=0 CAL=1 OK=1 is not a valid combination.

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_endianness_probe
invalidAndEdge.expectation: A correct little-endian receiver decodes 0x8403 = -31741 counts = -3174.1 deg, far outside the +/-780 deg range. A wrongly big-endian receiver decodes 900 counts = +90.0 deg.
invalidAndEdge.note: Byte-swapped twin of lws_plus90_100dps. Use it to prove byte order on real hardware.

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_config_zero_angle
invalidAndEdge.expectation: LWS_Config, CCW = 3h, sets LWS_Angle to 0 deg. VCU-to-sensor direction.

invalidAndEdge.name: lws_config_reset_calibration
invalidAndEdge.expectation: LWS_Config, CCW = 5h, resets the calibration status of the angle. VCU-to-sensor direction.
